subject: Request: Measurement horizon adjustment & temporary p95 offset for BrightLine
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@brightline.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: BrightLine Ops <ops@brightline.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed P95 spike after feature rollout — asking for temporary measurement window relief

Hi Rachel,

We rolled the new recommendation model for patient triage yesterday evening across ~20% of our Hosted traffic. Since then our internal monitoring shows p95 for "generate_text" calls has jumped from ~420ms to ~980ms during a narrow 14:00-16:00 PDT window. This aligns with the rollout, and our ops team is seeing repeated short-lived spikes that resolve in about 20-30 minutes but recur during that afternoon window.

We understand redwood's p95 commitment in the contract, and we want to avoid penalties while we stabilize the model configuration. Can BrightLine request a temporary p95 offset (e.g., provisional 1.2s p95 for a 7-calendar-day window) and a measurement-horizon adjustment for that region while we patch our prompts and model sizing? We can provide sample telemetry and are open to mitigation steps (traffic shaping/canary rollback) discussed below.

Attached is a small sample of our telemetry for the last 48h.

Thanks — looking for your guidance and the formal next steps.

— Elena
Head of Product, BrightLine

Attachments: brightline-latency-sample-20250621.csv (CSV stub, 120KB)

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Elena Martinez <elena@brightline.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed P95 spike after feature rollout — asking for temporary measurement window relief

Elena — thanks for the data and the clear ask. Short answer: we can offer a provisional SLO adjustment pathway, but we need a concrete mitigation plan and evidence so the change is timeboxed and reversible.

High level proposal:
- Temporary p95 derating to 1.2s for the US region for up to 7 calendar days, with daily telemetry reporting from BrightLine.
- Measurement-horizon tweak: exclude the 15-minute rolling windows that match your canary expansion windows for the duration of the exception. (This prevents brief rollout blips from triggering the quantile.)
- Mandatory remediation checkpoints at 48h and 120h with telemetry and a rollback/mitigation decision point.

Please confirm you can provide: telemetry with request ids, a short runbook for traffic shaping or rollback, and an internal owner for the restore decision. I'll loop in Ben for the evidence checklist and SLA paperwork.

I'll prepare the formal exception addendum (DocuSign) pending acceptance.

— Rachel
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Note: attaching sample exception template after Ben's input.

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, Elena Martinez <elena@brightline.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed P95 spike after feature rollout — asking for temporary measurement window relief

Elena / Rachel — I pulled aggregated telemetry from our edge and the Hosted routing logs around the periods you flagged. Couple of quick observations:

- The spike in p95 aligns with increased median sequence length on requests (we see a 2.3x jump in average input tokens in the 14:00-16:00 window). Longer sequences + concurrent canary batch = higher tail latency.
- There are intermittent queue depth spikes in our regional pool at the same time (short-lived backpressure).

I attached a compact evidence package with token distributions and sample request ids so BrightLine ops can map to their traces. If BrightLine can temporarily limit max tokens or route high-length requests to a dedicated route (we can provision a transient reserved queue), the p95 should recover faster than rolling back the model.

Suggested mitigation path (technical):
1) Immediately: provision a small reserved capacity route for high-length requests (2-4 gpus) — reversible within ~60 minutes.
2) Short term: apply a 7-day p95 offset of 1.2s with required telemetry uploads every 24h.
3) Re-eval at 48h: if token distribution normalizes and p95 drops <900ms persistently, we terminate exception early.

Attachments: slo-evidence-package-20250622.zip (contains token-distribution.csv, sample-reqids.txt)

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ops confirms that the longest sequences are the new demographic+history payloads from the recommender and we can throttle or truncate to a 1024-token cap in the short term. We prefer to avoid an immediate rollback since the newer model is performing better on quality metrics.

We accept the 7-day provisional p95 offset to 1.2s with the daily telemetry requirement. We'll submit the telemetry CSVs to the shared S3 folder you provide and will run the 48h checkpoint. Can you send the DocuSign addendum and the S3 path?

We'll also try the reserved route option — ops expects they can flip traffic in about 45 minutes once provisioned.

— Elena
